title: Agent Budgeting & Admission Control
summary: Reserve and enforce task-level limits for model tokens, tool calls, concurrency, elapsed time, and downstream load before work begins.
overview: Agent budgeting constrains the total resources a logical task may consume, including retries, parallel branches, and delegated subtasks. Admission control decides whether a new task can start under current capacity and policy. Together they prevent an apparently small request from expanding into unbounded model calls or overwhelming a dependent service.

A token rate limit alone does not govern a multi-step workflow. Track reserved and spent budget across the task tree, and distinguish capacity limits from monetary accounting. Estimates guide admission; runtime enforcement and reconciliation handle estimation error. When a budget is exhausted, return a useful partial result or explicit handoff rather than hiding unfinished work.

production.poc: A proof of concept records tokens, tool calls, and elapsed time per task to identify expansion patterns before defining enforceable budgets.
production.production: Production reserves capacity before dispatch, enforces per-task and per-tenant limits, bounds retries, and defines queueing, cancellation, and partial-result behavior.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds weighted fairness, priority classes, regional capacity, adaptive estimates, budget transfer rules, and reconciliation for delayed usage receipts.

components.name: Admission controller
components.role: Checks tenant policy, priority, available capacity, and estimated task cost before accepting work.

components.name: Budget ledger
components.role: Atomically tracks reservations, consumption, releases, and parent-child allocations across concurrent branches.

components.name: Execution governor
components.role: Enforces time, iteration, tool-call, and token limits during runtime rather than relying on model cooperation.

components.name: Priority queue
components.role: Schedules admitted tasks with fairness and explicit expiry under constrained capacity.

components.name: Usage reconciler
components.role: Matches estimated reservations with observed provider and tool usage, including late or failed calls.

flow.title: Estimate bounded demand
flow.description: Classify the task and calculate a conservative reservation from allowed steps, model choices, and tool costs.

flow.title: Apply admission policy
flow.description: Check tenant quota, priority, downstream concurrency, and regional capacity; queue or reject with a clear retry contract if unavailable.

flow.title: Reserve atomically
flow.description: Create a task budget and allocate child limits without allowing parallel workers to overspend the same remaining balance.

flow.title: Enforce during execution
flow.description: Charge every attempt, including retries and failed calls, and stop scheduling new work when any hard limit is reached.

flow.title: Degrade intentionally
flow.description: Choose an approved lower-cost path, return a labeled partial result, or hand off unresolved work without silently weakening required checks.

flow.title: Reconcile and release
flow.description: Replace estimates with observed usage, release unused reservations, and retain a cost and completion explanation for the task owner.

useCase.title: Alarm-storm investigation admission
useCase.situation: Illustrative architecture: A network incident creates thousands of related alarms and could trigger one investigation per event.
useCase.problem: Unbounded agent fan-out consumes model capacity and overloads diagnostic APIs precisely when operators need them most.
useCase.requirement: Admit incident-level work fairly, cap diagnostic load, and reserve capacity for higher-priority operational requests.
useCase.architecture: An admission controller groups related signals, reserves one investigation budget, and allocates bounded specialist branches against a shared ledger.
useCase.failure: A branch reaches its tool-call cap while evidence remains incomplete; the workflow returns the completed findings and routes unresolved checks to the operator.
useCase.impact: Measure cost per accepted investigation, queue delay, denied work, fairness by tenant, budget overruns, and task quality under constrained capacity.

tradeoffs.cost: Can leave capacity idle when estimates are too high.
Requires atomic coordination and clear allocation rules.
Needs starvation prevention and transparent treatment of lower-priority tasks.

failures.scenario: Parallel branches both observe the same remaining budget.
failures.detection: Ledger reconciliation detects reservations exceeding the parent cap.
failures.recovery: Use atomic reservation operations and stop unreserved work before further dispatch.

failures.scenario: A cancelled model call still incurs delayed usage.
failures.detection: Provider receipts arrive after the task has been marked cancelled.
failures.recovery: Charge the original task ledger and reconcile outstanding reservations before closing accounting.

mistakes.fix: Account for failed attempts, retries, tools, embeddings, and cancelled work with observed cost.

mistakes.mistake: Letting a specialist create unlimited child agents.
mistakes.fix: Require explicit child reservations drawn from the parent budget.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping verification steps first when money runs low.
mistakes.fix: Preserve mandatory checks and reduce scope or return a clearly incomplete result.

whenToUse: Agents can loop, retry, or delegate enough work to make resource use unpredictable.
Several tenants or priorities share constrained model and tool capacity.
The product needs an explicit cost and completion contract for each task.
whenNotToUse: A fixed deterministic request has negligible and already bounded resource use.
Budget policy would silently remove checks required for a valid result.
The implementation cannot reconcile usage across asynchronous branches and providers.
checklist: Define task, tenant, and platform limits for every meaningful resource.
Reserve parent and child budgets atomically before dispatch.
Include retries, failures, tools, and delayed receipts in accounting.
Specify queue fairness, priority, expiry, and rejection behavior.
Enforce hard limits outside the model and stop new work on exhaustion.
Design useful partial results and explicit unresolved-work handoffs.
Test parallel overspend, cancellation charges, and reservation leakage.
